questions.q: Identify a habit that keeps us healthy in body and mind.
questions.explain: Getting enough sleep rests the body and the mind. Long computer use, loud music and daily fast food all harm our health.

questions.q: We should eat regular, balanced meals. State what a balanced diet gives us.
choices: the nutrients and energy we need
questions.explain: A balanced diet gives us all the nutrients and energy we need, in the right amounts.

questions.q: Name the condition that long hours of loud music can cause.
questions.explain: Listening to loud music for long hours damages the ear and can cause deafness.

questions.q: A student uses a computer for hours without breaks. Identify what may be damaged.
questions.explain: Looking at a screen for hours without breaks strains the eyes and can damage eyesight.

questions.q: Name the substances found in large amounts in convenience food.
questions.explain: Convenience foods, such as fast food and instant noodles, often contain a lot of salt, sugar and saturated fats.

questions.q: Identify a health problem caused by eating convenience food often.
questions.explain: Convenience food often has a lot of salt and fat. Eating it often can lead to high blood pressure.

questions.q: A person has shoulder and back pain. Identify the likely cause.
questions.explain: Sitting at a computer for a long time without breaks, often with poor posture, strains the shoulders and back.

questions.q: BMI tells us if our weight is healthy. State the formula for BMI.
questions.explain: BMI is the mass in kilograms divided by the height in metres squared. So BMI = mass ÷ (height × height).

questions.q: State the unit of BMI.
questions.explain: BMI is mass in kg divided by height squared in m². So its unit is kg/m².

questions.q: A person has mass 80 kg. Height x height is 4 m². Calculate the BMI.
questions.explain: BMI = mass ÷ (height × height) = 80 kg ÷ 4 m² = 20 kg/m².

questions.q: A person has mass 44 kg. Height x height is 2 m². Calculate the BMI.
questions.explain: BMI = mass ÷ (height × height) = 44 kg ÷ 2 m² = 22 kg/m².

questions.q: A person has BMI 20 kg/m². Height x height is 2 m². Calculate the mass.
questions.explain: Mass = BMI × (height × height) = 20 kg/m² × 2 m² = 40 kg.

questions.q: A person has a BMI below 18.5. Identify the weight group.
questions.explain: A BMI below 18.5 is underweight.

questions.q: A person has a BMI of 32. Identify the weight group.
questions.explain: A BMI of 30 or more is obese. So a BMI of 32 is obese.

questions.q: A person has a BMI of 20. Identify the weight group.
questions.explain: A BMI from 18.5 to below 25 is a healthy weight. So a BMI of 20 is a healthy weight.

questions.q: Over-exercising means exercising far too much. Name a risk of over-exercising.
questions.explain: Exercising far too much does not give the body time to recover. This can injure the muscles and joints.

questions.q: Over-dieting means eating far too little. Name a risk of over-dieting.
questions.explain: Eating far too little means the body does not get the nutrients it needs. This is malnutrition.

questions.q: A person wants to lose weight safely. Identify the best way.
choices: eating only one type of food
questions.explain: The safe way to lose weight is to eat balanced meals and exercise regularly. Skipping meals or eating only one food can cause malnutrition.

questions.q: State the cause of influenza (flu).
questions.explain: Influenza (flu) is caused by viruses. It spreads from person to person through the air.

questions.q: State the cause of tuberculosis.
questions.explain: Tuberculosis is caused by bacteria. It mainly attacks the lungs.

questions.q: State the cause of thalassemia.
questions.explain: Thalassemia is a hereditary disease. It is passed on through the genes from the parents.

questions.q: State the cause of SARS.
questions.explain: SARS is caused by a virus.

questions.q: Identify the disease caused by a virus.
questions.explain: AIDS is caused by a virus called HIV. Syphilis and tuberculosis are caused by bacteria, and colour blindness is hereditary.

questions.q: Hereditary diseases are passed on from parents. Identify the hereditary disease.
questions.explain: Colour blindness is passed on from parents through their genes, so it is hereditary. SARS, influenza and tuberculosis are caused by germs.

questions.q: Name the germ-killing chemical used to clean a floor.
questions.explain: A disinfectant is a strong chemical that kills germs on objects and surfaces, such as floors. It is too harsh to use on skin.

questions.q: Name the germ-killing chemical used to wash our hands.
questions.explain: An antiseptic is a mild chemical that kills germs on the skin. It is safe to wash our hands with.

questions.q: A doctor gives medicine to kill bacteria inside the body. Name this medicine.
questions.explain: An antibiotic is a medicine that kills bacteria inside the body.

questions.q: Identify where a disinfectant should be used.
choices: on a cut on the skin
questions.explain: Disinfectants are used on objects and surfaces such as a kitchen table. They are too harsh for skin or for use inside the body.

questions.q: Name the germs that antibiotics kill.
questions.explain: Antibiotics kill bacteria. They do not work against viruses.

questions.q: Hands are washed in different ways. Identify the way that removes the most bacteria.
questions.explain: Antiseptic soap kills germs as well as washing them off. So it removes the most bacteria.

questions.q: Vaccination is given before we fall sick. State what it protects us from.
questions.explain: A vaccination prepares the body to fight a particular disease before we catch it. It protects us from certain diseases, such as those caused by some viruses, but not from all diseases.

questions.q: Name the method that protects us from certain viruses.
questions.explain: Vaccination protects us from certain viruses. Antibiotics kill bacteria, and disinfectants and antiseptics kill germs outside the body.

questions.q: A doctor gives a full course of antibiotics. Explain why we must finish it.
questions.explain: Stopping antibiotics early can leave some bacteria alive. These bacteria can multiply and make the person sick again.

questions.q: A boy stops his antibiotics too early. Predict what may happen.
choices: he may become protected from viruses
questions.explain: If the antibiotics are stopped too early, some bacteria may survive and multiply. The boy may fall sick again.

questions.q: Thalassemia is a hereditary disease. State how a hereditary disease is passed on.
questions.explain: A hereditary disease is passed on from parents to children through their genes.

questions.q: In thalassemia, a faulty gene affects red blood cells. Describe what happens to them.
questions.explain: In thalassemia, a faulty gene makes the red blood cells weak, and they are destroyed. The person does not have enough red blood cells.

questions.q: A mother has thalassemia. Explain why her children may have it.
choices: it is passed on in genes
it comes from a poor diet
questions.explain: Thalassemia is a hereditary disease. The faulty gene can be passed on from the mother to her children.

questions.q: Kidney dialysis helps people whose kidneys have failed. State what it does.
choices: does the work of the kidney
questions.explain: Kidney dialysis does the work of the kidneys. It removes wastes from the blood.

questions.q: State one problem with kidney dialysis.
choices: it puts in a new kidney
questions.explain: Dialysis does not cure kidney failure. It is not permanent, so the patient must have it again and again.

questions.q: A patient gets a new kidney. Explain why the patient needs long-term medicine.
choices: to stop the body rejecting it
questions.explain: The body may attack a new kidney as something foreign. Long-term medicine stops the body from rejecting it.
